content: To measure the similarity between a class word subspace ${Y}_c$ and a query word subspace ${Y}_q$ , the canonical angles between the two word subspaces are used BIBREF21 . There are several methods for calculating canonical angles BIBREF22 , BIBREF23 , and BIBREF24 , among which the simplest and most practical is the singular value decomposition (SVD). Consider, for example, two subspaces, one from the training data and another from the query, represented as matrices of bases, ${Y}_{c} = [{\Phi }_{1} \ldots {\Phi }_{m_c}] \in \mathbb {R}^{p \times m_c}$ and ${Y}_{q} = [{\Psi }_{1} \ldots {\Psi }_{m_q}] \in \mathbb {R}^{p \times m_q}$ , where ${\Phi }_{i}$ are the bases for ${Y}_c$ and ${\Psi }_{i}$ are the bases for ${Y}_q$ . Let the SVD of ${Y}_c^{\top }{Y}_q \in \mathbb {R}^{m_c \times m_q}$ be ${Y}_c^{\top }{Y}_q = {U \Sigma V}^{\top }$ , where ${Y}_q$0 , ${Y}_q$1 represents the set of singular values. The canonical angles ${Y}_q$2 can be obtained as ${Y}_q$3 ${Y}_q$4 . The similarity between the two subspaces is measured by ${Y}_q$5 angles as follows:
